text:
alex: kicking off a canary for model v2.3-quant4 with rate-aware debounce. starting at 5% traffic for 30m. primary gates: MRR, hallucination_rate, latency_p95. autofallback rule: MRR_drop >= 1.5% (absolute) AND hallucination_rate_increase >= 0.4% OR latency_p95 > 1200ms for 2 consecutive 5m windows.

deploy-bot: Canary started for v2.3-quant4 -> 5% traffic. dashboard: https://console.redwood/testing/canary/1732501234 :rocket:

maria: noted. i'll seed synthetic bursts for short periods to validate rate sensitivity. planning bursts at 1.2x, 2x, 3x baseline QPS.

sam: quick q: the MRR threshold is absolute vs relative? should we use absolute to match user impact?
alex: absolute. small percent changes still matter for top-k ranking. relative introduces weirdness for low-base slices.

jing: propose we add a debounce that requires two failing windows within 15m and also a qps-normalized check (ignore if qps > 2x unless MRR drop > 3%). avoids noisy spikes causing autofallback.
sam: makes sense. can we express the qps normalization as `if qps_multiplier > 2 then require MRR_drop >= 3%`?

alex: yes, exactly. also log sample ids for failing slices to s3://redwood-canary/artifacts/1732501234/ so we can debug prompts.

maria: ran the 1.2x burst shadow -> MRR delta = -0.4%, hallucination +0.05%, latency p95 +80ms. 2x burst -> MRR delta -1.6%, hallucination +0.45%, p95 +220ms. 3x -> MRR -2.8%, hallucination +0.9%. attaching quick blocks:
```
slice, qps_mult, mrr_delta, halluc_delta, p95_delta
longform_docs,1.2,-0.4,0.05,80ms
longform_docs,2.0,-1.6,0.45,220ms
conversation_short,2.0,-0.6,0.02,90ms
```

sam: interesting — degradation concentrated in longform_docs slice at >1.5x QPS. probably kv-cache warmup and decoder throughput.

jing: for this canary we should enable rate-aware debounce: treat failures as only actionable if qps_mult <= 2 OR absolute MRR_drop >= 3%. i'll add rule to canary config.

alex: also set a soft-promote step: if stable at 5% for 30m, promote to 20% with a 60m watch and stricter gating (same MRR threshold but require 60m consecutive stability).

deploy-bot: Canary updated: v2.3-quant4 -> promoted to 20% (watch=60m). Current metrics: MRR_delta=-0.5%, hallucination=+0.08%, p95=+95ms.

maria: running a 20% run with two 2x bursts; results so far: overall MRR -0.7% (within 1.5%), but longform_docs slice still -1.9% during 2x bursts.

sam: can we fallback just the longform_docs route instead of full model? route-level fallback would minimize user impact.
alex: yes — routing supports per-route fallbacks. set route-fallback for `longform_docs` to v2.2-fp16 if longform MRR_drop >= 1.5% for two windows.
jing: implemented and tested in staging. config snippet: 
```yaml
auto_fallback:
  global_thresholds:
    mrr_abs_drop: 1.5
    windows: 2
  route_overrides:
    longform_docs:
      fallback_to: v2.2-fp16
      mrr_abs_drop: 1.5
```

alex: final decision: keep v2.3-quant4 at 20% with route-level fallback on longform_docs. enable rate-aware debounce (ignore failures above 2x qps unless MRR_drop >= 3%). autobackstop: full rollback if global MRR_drop >= 1.5% and hallucination +0.5% sustained.

jing: i'll carve out an alert in pager for the route-level fallback and add an entry to the runbook.
maria: i'll collect the sample traces and run an int4-specific kv-warmup patch to try to fix longform.
sam: i'll draft a short postmortem note if route fallback fires.

alex: thanks team. will follow up with canary dashboard link and postmortem if any autofallbacks trigger. closing thread for now. :white_check_mark:
